hook.text: You load 100 blog posts, then for each post, run a query to load the author. That's 101 queries.

buildup.text: The N+1 problem occurs when code fetches a list, then queries for related data one item at a time.

discovery.text: The fix is eager loading: one query for posts, one query for all related authors. Two queries instead of 101.

twist.text: ORMs often hide N+1 problems. The code looks clean, but the generated SQL is catastrophically inefficient.

climax.text: N+1 queries are the most common performance bug in web applications. Always check your ORM's query log.

punchline.text: One query for the list, one for the relations — not one per item.

quiz.question: What causes the N+1 query problem?
options: Querying for related data one item at a time instead of in batch
